causal-factors.name: Franchise-driven 2026 release slate
causal-factors.rationale: Gower Street Analytics and Variety note a calendar packed with new installments from Avengers, Spider-Man, Toy Story, Dune, Star Wars, Super Mario Bros, Minions, Jumanji, Scream, The Fockers, and The Hunger Games, which collectively raise the odds of at least one title crossing $1B worldwide.

causal-factors.name: Recent 1B box-office breakthroughs (2025)
causal-factors.rationale: AP News reports Zootopia 2 surpassed $1.14B and Lilo & Stitch crossed $1B in 2025, demonstrating that the billion-dollar milestone remained attainable in the current market.

causal-factors.name: Global box office growth forecast for 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Industry projections (Variety via Gower Street Analytics) estimate global box office at about $35B in 2026, implying a favorable environment for multi-year box office performers to break the $1B mark.

causal-factors.name: Finite base rate of 1B films
causal-factors.rationale: Historically only a limited subset of films reach $1B worldwide, with the club comprising a finite number of titles, which tempers the odds even in a strong year.

causal-factors.name: International market growth driven by Hollywood product
causal-factors.rationale: Forecasts emphasize growth in regions where Hollywood franchises perform strongly, increasing the probability that a tentpole could break the $1B barrier globally.

causal-factors.name: China market uncertainty could dampen upside
causal-factors.rationale: Historical coverage notes China’s slower reception to some mega-hits; continued uncertainty there could temper the global upside required to reach $1B in some cases.

causal-factors.name: Avatar: Fire and Ash milestone (global 1B+)
causal-factors.rationale: Avatar: Fire and Ash surpassed $1B worldwide by early January 2026, demonstrating that a 1B global milestone can occur within the 2025–26 slate. (Box Office Mojo; Forbes)

causal-factors.name: 2026 global box office headroom
causal-factors.rationale: Forecasts indicate global box office could reach around $35B in 2026, implying sufficient scale for at least one film to cross the $1B threshold. (The Numbers; Yahoo)

causal-factors.name: Recent 1B blockbusters establish durable trend
causal-factors.rationale: Barbie (2023), Inside Out 2 (2024), and Zootopia 2 (2025) crossed $1B, illustrating a durable trajectory for 1B global box office in recent years. (TheWrap; Bloomberg; Box Office Mojo)

causal-factors.name: Holdovers from 2025 boosting 2026 slate
causal-factors.rationale: The Numbers projects 2026 will include holdovers from 2025 such as Avatar: Fire and Ash and Zootopia 2, contributing meaningfully to yearly totals. (The Numbers)

causal-factors.name: Strong international franchise tailwinds
causal-factors.rationale: Long-running, globally appealing franchises with broad international reach create favorable conditions for at least one title to exceed $1B. (AP News; Forbes)

causal-factors.name: Downside risk from streaming competition and ticket price pressure
causal-factors.rationale: Industry analyses flag streaming competition and higher ticket prices as headwinds that could dampen theatrical demand and limit 1B outcomes. (Forbes)

causal-factors.name: Risk of sequels saturation and market fatigue
causal-factors.rationale: Industry commentary cautions that an oversaturated slate of sequels may reduce the number of films able to reach $1B in a given year. (Forbes)

causal-factors.name: Avatar: Fire and Ash crossed $1B worldwide (as of January 4, 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: The milestone was reached within about two weeks of release, showing a 2025 tentpole can achieve $1B globally and increasing the likelihood that at least one film hits $1B by May 1, 2026. Sources: TheWrap (Jan 4, 2026); Forbes (Jan 4, 2026); Box Office Mojo (Jan 2026).

causal-factors.name: Disney's 2025 billion-dollar club momentum
causal-factors.rationale: Disney had three films crossing $1B in 2025 (including Lilo & Stitch and Zootopia 2), signaling sustained capacity to deliver 1B titles into 2026. Sources: TheWrap (Jan 4, 2026); AP News (Jan 2026).

causal-factors.name: Strong contributions from the China market to 1B-type outcomes
causal-factors.rationale: China’s performance for major releases (e.g., Zootopia 2, Ne Zha 2) has been a meaningful driver of global totals, supporting the probability of a 1B film by May 1, 2026. Sources: AP News (Jan 2026); TheWrap (Jan 2026).

causal-factors.name: Early-2026 box office signals show at least one 1B film already achieved
causal-factors.rationale: Early 2026 data confirm a 1B milestone for at least one film, which reduces uncertainty but does not guarantee additional 1B titles before May 1. Sources: Forbes (Jan 2026); TheWrap (Jan 2026).

synthesis: Despite credible headwinds, the appearance of a 1B milestone in early 2026 and a strong 2026 slate elevate the odds of at least one film crossing $1B worldwide. The probability is set to 0.97 with a 93–99% plausible range to reflect remaining uncertainties.
